description.narrative:
We will pilot an innovative, youth-led model to improve healthcare access for Deaf youth in Tanzania. Building on the European SignON project, we will adapt AI-supported sign language tools and low-tech visual aids to the Tanzanian context. Deaf and hearing youthwill be trained as Digital Health Navigators, equipped with Sexual and Reproductive Health knowledge, inclusive communication skills, and digital tools. The pilot will run at Buguruni Viziwi Primary School and the Audiology Department of Muhimbili University, engaging medical students and at least 200 Deaf youth. Activities include co-design labs, tool development, navigator training, and monthly learning sessions. Outputs will include an Open Toolkit and policy brief to support national scaling. This project prioritises girls with disabilities, strengthens youth leadership, and creates a replicable model for disability-inclusive healthcare across Africa and Europe.
The project aims to improve inclusive access to healthcare for Deaf youth by piloting a youth-led digital health navigation model. Our goal is to ensure Deaf young people can independently access healthcare services with dignity.
Objectives: 1. Developing AI-supported and low-tech communication tools in Tanzanian Sign Language, 2. Training 15 Deaf and hearing youth as DigitalHealth Navigators. 3. Testing the model at Buguruni Viziwi Primary School and Muhimbili University.
Activities cover co-design labs, tool development, navigator training, pilot deployment with 200 Deaf youth, and knowledge sharing through toolkits, case studies,and joint webinars with European partners.

participating-org.narrative:
Vijana Life Organization (VILO) is a youth‑led NGO founded in 2020 and accredited by the Registrar of NGOs in Tanzania (00NGO/R/1497). Since its inception, VILO has reached over 20,000 young people nationwide, addressing critical needs and driving positive change.
Vision: To become the primary organization supporting the youth of Tanzania.
Mission: To empower youth to advance sustainable health, education, and development, strengthening their social impact.
Core Values: Leadership, Innovation, Excellency, Volunteerism.
Objectives:
Expand economic opportunities by training 1,000 youth annually in entrepreneurship and livelihoods. Improve health and well‑being by reaching 5,000 youth each year with SRHR, mental health, and disease prevention programs. Enhance education through mentorship, leadership, and technology integration, supporting at least 200 youth annually. Promote environmental conservation by engaging youth in campaigns, research, and climate action. Focus Areas:
Good Health and Well‑Being: Empowering youth with SRHR knowledge, mental health awareness, and disease prevention. Support for Vulnerable Groups: Ensuring access to resources for people with disabilities, low‑income families, and marginalized communities. Quality Education: Expanding STEM, vocational, and digital literacyopportunities, especially for girls. No Poverty: Providing financial literacy, vocational training, and entrepreneurship support tostrengthen livelihoods. Gender Equality: Advocating against GBV, empowering girls, and eliminating disparities in education, health, and employment. Life on Land: Building youth climate scientists, raising awareness, and promoting resilience through environmentalaction.
Through innovation, collaboration, and youth leadership, VILO is building a healthier, more equitable, and sustainable future for Tanzania’s young people.
